subject: Banking
title: Credit Freezes and Fraud Alerts
description: A 60-second lesson on Credit Freezes and Fraud Alerts.

hook.text: A credit freeze blocks anyone from opening accounts in your name. After the Equifax breach, freezes became free by law.

buildup.text: Without a freeze, a thief with your Social Security number can open credit cards, loans, and utilities in your name.

discovery.text: You must freeze your credit at all three bureaus separately. Freezing one leaves two others open for fraud.

twist.text: A fraud alert only lasts one year and just asks lenders to verify identity. A freeze actually blocks access entirely.

climax.text: Credit freezes are the most effective identity theft prevention. They're free, reversible, and work immediately.

punchline.text: Free, instant, and the best identity theft protection. Freeze all three bureaus.

quiz.question: What does a credit freeze do?
options: Blocks anyone from opening new accounts in your name

details.summary: A credit freeze locks your credit file so no one can open new accounts in your name, while a fraud alert requires lenders to verify your identity before approving credit. Both are free tools that protect against identity theft.
details.whyItMatters: After major data breaches exposing hundreds of millions of records, credit freezes are the single most effective defense against identity theft. They prevent criminals from opening fraudulent accounts even with your stolen personal information.
takeaways: A freeze prevents all new credit from being opened in your name
Freezes are free to place and lift at all three major credit bureaus
Fraud alerts require lenders to take extra steps to verify your identity

faq.question: What is the difference between a freeze and a lock?
faq.answer: A freeze is a legal right under federal law, free at all bureaus. A lock is a bureau product that offers similar protection but may carry fees and operates under different legal terms. Freezes provide stronger legal protections.

faq.question: Does a credit freeze affect your existing accounts?
faq.answer: No. A freeze only prevents new accounts from being opened. Your existing credit cards, loans, and bank accounts function normally. Current creditors can still access your report for account management purposes.
